sentences: A locally decodable binary code allows recovery of any message bit from only a constant number of codeword queries.
The textbook asks whether such codes can have blocklength polynomial in the message length.
The decoder must tolerate corruption without scanning the entire stored representation.
Polynomial length would make strong locality compatible with a much more economical redundancy cost.
The saved note does not state the corruption fraction, success probability, or fixed query count, so these constants must be chosen explicitly before comparing construction and lower-bound regimes.
